prompt: A claims assistant produces fluent citations, but a reviewed sample shows occasional invented docket numbers. The team proposes a stronger style prompt. Which architectural response addresses the decisive model property?

options.text: Treat generated names as uncertain; resolve docket IDs against an authoritative registry and evaluate exact-match errors across representative cases.
Add more examples and accept the citation whenever the explanation is coherent.
Ask a second model to confirm each identifier without checking an authoritative source.
Raise the output token limit so the model has more room to reason about the docket.

feedback.reason: Fluent next-token generation does not establish that a precise identifier is valid; use an authoritative deterministic check for the identifier.

details.mechanismOrProperty: The model generates plausible continuations and can be wrong on precise facts; architecture should put authoritative data or deterministic validation on exact factual fields.
details.scenarioApplication: Fluent next-token generation does not establish that a precise identifier is valid; use an authoritative deterministic check for the identifier.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: A prompt may improve behavior, but it cannot turn generated text into an authoritative registry value.
details.errorCorrection: Separate a plausible factual string from an identifier verified against its authoritative registry.
details.transfer: Identify which output properties require grounded authority or exact validation rather than relying on fluency.

messages.text: Coherent prose and more examples do not establish that a docket ID exists in the registry.
A second model can repeat the same plausible error. Check the identifier against its authoritative source.
More output capacity supplies no new docket evidence; the exact identifier still needs a registry check.

course.title: Module 1 · Claude Platform & Solution Design: Architect
course.section: M1-S02: The four properties architects design around; M1-S07: Where Claude fits (Claude / systems / humans)

prompt: A summarization service meets average quality goals but produces different omissions on repeated runs for the same long case file. Release approval currently uses one run per case. What is the strongest adjustment?

options.text: Increase the context window and assume repeatability improves as the full file fits.
Run the same prompt once more only when the first summary looks unusually short.
Make temperature zero and treat the resulting output as deterministic proof.
Evaluate repeated runs across representative long and short cases, track omission variance, and set a release threshold for the risky fields.

feedback.reason: The observed failure is run-to-run variability and the release test undersamples it; repeated representative evaluation measures the property that threatens reliability.

details.mechanismOrProperty: Non-determinism means repeated identical inputs can yield different outputs; evaluation must characterize variation, not infer it from one trial.
details.scenarioApplication: The observed failure is run-to-run variability and the release test undersamples it; repeated representative evaluation measures the property that threatens reliability.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: A low-variance result does not guarantee factuality or safety, so retain separate factual and policy checks.
details.errorCorrection: Measure repeated omissions by relevant field and case type; one successful run or a sampling parameter is not a reliability proof.
details.transfer: Choose an evaluation design that measures the source of uncertainty rather than changing an unrelated capacity setting.

messages.text: Fitting a larger file may address missing context, but it does not measure the observed run-to-run omission variance.
Length-triggered reruns exclude fluent summaries that still omit risky fields and do not characterize representative variance.
A low-temperature setting is not evidence that every required field is reliably retained; evaluate repeated task outcomes.

course.title: Module 1 · Claude Platform & Solution Design: Architect
course.section: M1-S02: The four properties architects design around; M1-S07: Where Claude fits (Claude / systems / humans)

prompt: A natural-language triage assistant sometimes follows a reviewer’s requested format and sometimes adds an unrequested paragraph. The output must satisfy a strict downstream JSON schema. What should the architect do?

options.text: Use the model for interpretation, then validate the response against a schema and reject or repair invalid structure before downstream use.
Strengthen the prompt until formatting appears consistent, then pass responses directly to the parser.
Ask reviewers to manually remove extra paragraphs after the service has acted on the response.
Treat format adherence as a model-training issue and postpone release until a future model version.

feedback.reason: Steerability can improve formatting but is not a hard contract; a parser-facing schema needs deterministic validation and an explicit failure path.

details.mechanismOrProperty: The model can be guided by prompts but may deviate. Application-owned validators enforce exact structural requirements.
details.scenarioApplication: Steerability can improve formatting but is not a hard contract; a parser-facing schema needs deterministic validation and an explicit failure path.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Schema validity does not prove the underlying extracted values are correct; validate both as separate properties.
details.errorCorrection: Parse and validate before downstream use, then return an explicit repair or failure state for an invalid response.
details.transfer: Use natural-language steering for behavior and deterministic checks for requirements whose violation breaks the system.

messages.text: Prompt consistency in a few trials does not enforce a downstream schema. Validate before the response is consumed.
Cleanup after the service acts is too late to protect the downstream structure contract.
Application validation can enforce the required structure now; waiting for a future model does not define a safe failure path.

course.title: Module 1 · Claude Platform & Solution Design: Architect
course.section: M1-S02: The four properties architects design around; M1-S07: Where Claude fits (Claude / systems / humans)

prompt: A financial assistant must classify a request into one of four supported account actions. The model is broadly helpful but occasionally invents a fifth action that the ledger does not support. Which design best respects the model’s limits?

options.text: Ask for a longer chain of reasoning and let the assistant decide whether a fifth action is useful.
Use a larger context budget so all historical account activity is available before choosing.
Constrain the action field to the four supported values and have the application reject any value outside the ledger contract.
Tell the model that it is highly steerable and should never produce unsupported actions.

feedback.reason: The ledger contract is an explicit finite rule, so the application must enforce the allowed action set even if prompting lowers violations.

details.mechanismOrProperty: Steerability is useful but not equivalent to deterministic enforcement; the finite domain belongs in code or schema validation.
details.scenarioApplication: The ledger contract is an explicit finite rule, so the application must enforce the allowed action set even if prompting lowers violations.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: A valid action enum still requires authorization and business-rule checks before a consequential ledger update.
details.errorCorrection: Reject an unsupported action value in the application; even an allowed value still needs authorization and business validation.
details.transfer: Map each model property to a corresponding architectural control and keep application invariants outside the model.

messages.text: The ledger supports four actions; longer reasoning cannot authorize an unsupported fifth operation.
More account history may help interpretation but does not change the finite action domain.
A steering instruction cannot replace the application’s allowed-value check.

course.title: Module 1 · Claude Platform & Solution Design: Architect
course.section: M1-S02: The four properties architects design around; M1-S07: Where Claude fits (Claude / systems / humans)

prompt: A courier assistant repeats yesterday’s pickup cutoff after operations changed a private cutoff table today. An authorized read-only tool can return the applicable table revision and effective time for the depot. Which design supplies the needed knowledge?

options.text: Query the authorized table for the depot and applicable time, retain its revision, and explain that result; report unavailable if the lookup fails.
Use the model’s learned courier knowledge and add a confidence score to its cutoff estimate.
Ask another model whether yesterday’s cutoff still sounds plausible before responding.
Keep yesterday’s cutoff until a user complains, because a prompt update would be cheaper than a tool call.

feedback.reason: The private changing table is the authority. Model confidence or agreement cannot establish today’s effective cutoff.

details.mechanismOrProperty: Knowledge boundaries require an external source of truth for private or changing facts.
details.scenarioApplication: Read the depot-specific effective record and preserve its revision instead of mixing current and historic cutoffs.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: A failed lookup remains unavailable; do not silently fall back to an old cutoff.
details.errorCorrection: Confidence and another model do not update private facts. Retrieve the applicable authoritative revision before asserting the cutoff.
details.transfer: When a fact depends on a private or changing record, identify its authority and applicable version before answering.

messages.text: Training knowledge and a confidence label do not reveal a private change made today.
Model agreement is not a lookup of the depot’s current authoritative revision.
Waiting for complaints knowingly serves a stale value and does not satisfy the current-fact task.

course.title: Module 1 · Claude Platform & Solution Design: Architect
course.section: M1-S02: The four properties architects design around

prompt: A training assistant explains the difference between a JSON object and array using synthetic examples supplied in the prompt. It makes no claim about a current product release, private policy or account. Representative evaluation meets the required explanation and example-validity floors. Which approach fits this bounded task?

options.text: Require live web retrieval for every explanation because model knowledge can never be useful.
Use a bounded explanation prompt and retain the evaluated quality checks; add retrieval only if the task later needs current or external facts.
Load the organization’s private policy corpus before explaining the supplied examples.
Treat the passed evaluation as a guarantee that every later product or account question needs no verification.

feedback.reason: Stable generic concepts and supplied examples can support a bounded evaluated response. External authority is needed when the task actually depends on it, not for every use of model knowledge.

details.mechanismOrProperty: The same knowledge property permits useful common-pattern explanation while limiting claims about rare, private or fast-changing facts.
details.scenarioApplication: Keep the synthetic examples and evaluation scope explicit.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Reassess source needs when the requested fact or task changes.
details.errorCorrection: Do not turn uncertainty about some facts into a requirement to retrieve every stable explanation. Use the supplied task evidence and measured quality gates.
details.transfer: Separate stable general explanation from claims needing current or private evidence.

messages.text: A blanket retrieval rule adds cost without a missing current fact in this evaluated task.
Private policy adds irrelevant context to the synthetic JSON explanation.
This evaluation covers the stated explanation task; it does not validate unrelated current or private facts.

course.title: Module 1 · Claude Platform & Solution Design: Architect
course.section: M1-S02: The four properties architects design around

prompt: For this exercise, request admission requires input plus reserved output to fit within a 64,000-token window. Mandatory case evidence uses 40,000 tokens, tool definitions 12,000, old conversation 14,000, and required output reserve 4,000. A reviewed 2,000-token replacement for the old conversation preserves every required prior decision and source reference. Which admission decision fits?

options.text: Send the 70,000-token plan and let generation decide which material to omit.
Drop 12,000 tokens from mandatory current evidence without checking which facts are lost.
Use the reviewed history replacement, recount the full request and reserve, then admit the 58,000-token plan while retaining links to the original history.
Increase only the output-token setting because more generated text restores missing input capacity.

feedback.reason: The original plan totals 70,000 tokens. Replacing only the reviewed history reduces it to 58,000 including output reserve, preserving mandatory evidence and tool definitions under the stated exercise policy.

details.mechanismOrProperty: Working memory is finite; account for every input component and the required output reserve before admission.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: The reviewed summary is a case premise, not a claim that arbitrary compression always preserves every required fact.
details.errorCorrection: Count the admitted components after replacement, including reserved output. More output capacity cannot repair an oversized input plan.
details.transfer: Before admitting a request, account for mandatory input and output reserve; validate what any summary preserves.

messages.text: The original plan exceeds the explicit admission limit; silent omission is not an acceptable way to select evidence.
Mandatory facts cannot be discarded merely to fit the window. The exercise supplies an approved reducible history instead.
A larger output reserve consumes more window capacity and cannot restore input that was omitted.

course.title: Module 1 · Claude Platform & Solution Design: Architect
course.section: M1-S02: The four properties architects design around

prompt: A case conversation was compacted. The active context retains a reference to the approved deadline record but not the deadline value; the exact value is required in the next draft. An authorized case-record lookup is available. What should the application do?

options.text: Ask the model to remember the omitted turn and use the most plausible deadline.
Fetch the exact applicable deadline record, attach its version to the draft evidence, and stop or request review if it cannot be resolved.
Raise the maximum output length so the model can recover the earlier conversation.
Use the general deadline pattern learned from other cases and omit the uncertainty marker.

feedback.reason: A reference is a way to reload evidence, not the missing fact itself. Content outside active context should be recovered from the authoritative record rather than guessed.

details.mechanismOrProperty: Progressive context loading can recover the exact evidence needed at the next step.
details.scenarioApplication: Resolve the retained record reference before drafting the deadline.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Keep an explicit unresolved state when the authorized record is unavailable.
details.errorCorrection: An omitted fact is not restored by a longer completion or confident recall. Fetch the approved source value or expose its absence.
details.transfer: After compaction, distinguish a source reference from the source fact actually available to the model.

messages.text: The omitted value is not available merely because it appeared earlier in a conversation.
Output capacity does not reload input evidence that is absent from active context.
A pattern from other cases cannot establish this approved case-specific deadline.

course.title: Module 1 · Claude Platform & Solution Design: Architect
course.section: M1-S02: The four properties architects design around

prompt: A notice-drafting service produces different wording on repeated representative runs. Every run preserves the required facts, passes the structure and citation checks, and meets the agreed tone rubric. The contract does not require identical wording. What should determine release?

options.text: Reject the service solely because repeated outputs differ byte for byte.
Set a fixed sampling parameter and skip future field and citation checks.
Choose whichever run is longest because more text is evidence of completeness.
Judge the required facts, structure, citations and tone across the evaluated runs; allow wording variation within those gates and keep monitoring it.

feedback.reason: Variation is a property to evaluate against the task contract, not an automatic failure. Here the measured invariants pass and identical wording is not required.

details.mechanismOrProperty: Non-determinism requires repeated outcome evaluation while allowing harmless variation.
details.scenarioApplication: The notice wording varies but all stated release gates pass.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Reopen the decision if future variance changes required facts or other contractual outcomes.
details.errorCorrection: Changing wording is not itself a failed requirement. Judge each representative run against the stated critical fields and quality floors.
details.transfer: Define which output properties must remain invariant and which variations the task permits.

messages.text: Byte identity is not a requirement of this task; rejecting any variation ignores the measured accepted outcomes.
A parameter setting does not replace the required factual and structural checks.
Length does not establish the required facts or citation support.

course.title: Module 1 · Claude Platform & Solution Design: Architect
course.section: M1-S02: The four properties architects design around

prompt: An account assistant returns valid JSON with the supported action close_account. The current caller has read-only access, and the application authorization check denies closure. Which boundary applies?

options.text: Deny execution and explain the authorization result; valid structure and action membership do not grant the caller write permission.
Execute because the action is one of the ledger’s supported values.
Ask the model to confirm its confidence and execute if it remains certain.
Raise the model tier so the same valid JSON can serve as authorization.

feedback.reason: Schema validity, allowed-value membership and current authorization are distinct checks. The application must enforce the denied permission before any account mutation.

details.mechanismOrProperty: Steerability can produce the requested shape; application checks still enforce consequential invariants.
details.scenarioApplication: The current closure check is denied even though close_account is a valid enum value.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: A later permitted call requires a new current authorization check, not reusing this denied result.
details.errorCorrection: A well-formed action name establishes neither caller permission nor approval. Enforce the current authorization decision in application code.
details.transfer: Validate shape, allowed values and authority as separate conditions before executing an action.

messages.text: An operation can exist in the API without being permitted for this caller.
Model certainty does not change the application’s authorization decision.
Model capability cannot grant a read-only caller write authority.
